issues.reason: Gap territory: an abstract bare nominal inside a `For` oblique has no witness to hang `easy` on, and both emitted atoms are true of the compound and well-typed (`identification` is the head-noun genus; `easy` is a gradable adjective predicable of the referent, which the modifier-genus rule licenses), so this is graceful improvisation, not a false or over-asserting atom.

The distributive rule the issue invokes requires a group witness, which a non-specific bare-plural object inside a `Directive` seal does not have (the instruction set reserves the bare class symbol for exactly such generic objects), and the alternatives are worse — `(Inheritance container clear)` would be a false generic and dropping `clear` would lose stated content — so the two true, well-typed fusion atoms stand.

gaps_confirmed: gerund complement of a matrix verb ("consider using X") — the non-finite-complement pattern is stated for to-infinitive control verbs and causative bare/participle complements only

a descriptive adjective on a non-specific bare-plural object or on an abstract nominal in an oblique: fusion is barred for incidental description, there is no witness to predicate it of, and an `Inheritance` on the kind would assert a false generic
new_gaps: an abstract nominalization as the object of a purpose "for"-phrase ("for easy identification") has no reification route, so the underlying identifying event and its participants (identifying the leftovers) are unrecoverable

whether a purpose/connective relation atom (here `(To sk_use_1 sk_store_1)`) belongs inside or outside a `Directive` seal is unstated — the sealing section only fixes where definite-referent typing atoms go
notes: The `Directive` seal, the tenseless complement chain, the omitted addressee and the top-level typing of the definite "the fridge" all follow the instruction set. Both filed issues object to fusions that the parser used to carry stated content that has no other licensed carrier.
